bullets.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as NVDA CEO — Stock Hits 52-Week Low, Sector Selloff Ensues
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA President, CEO, and board member effective immediately following reports of an undisclosed relationship with a subordinate; CFO Colette Kress named Interim CEO while board searches for permanent successor. NVDA fell ~10% premarket to ~$155-161, hitting a 52-week low (-16.7% YTD), dragging AI infrastructure broadly lower: SMCI -9.3%, DELL -7.4%, CRWV -14.4%. Analyst PTs range widely — KeyBanc $150, JPM $215, Citi $225, DA Davidson $200 — with key risks centered on China revenue (~8-20% of sales), political pressure for tighter export controls, and loss of Huang's AI ecosystem relationships.

bullets.title: DOJ Pursues Multiple Antitrust Probes Into NVIDIA; Alice Huang/DeepSeek Link Compounds Risk
bullets.body: The DOJ is pursuing antitrust probes directly targeting NVIDIA, Supermicro, and Megaspeed, with Alice Huang's involvement a focus; the Commerce Department's Megaspeed investigation was transferred to DOJ after NVIDIA's general counsel inquired about the probe. Separately, Alice Huang-related companies invested in DeepSeek, which is promising NVIDIA Blackwell chips, adding a governance/conflict-of-interest dimension to the leadership crisis. No criminal charges against Huang or NVIDIA are indicated at this stage.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Succession: Ian Buck Leads at 37% Odds; AMD Voted #1 New Money Buy Post-News
bullets.body: Prediction markets show Ian Buck leading NVDA CEO succession odds at 37%, followed by Colette Kress at 26%; MS notes internal candidates include Jeff Fisher and Chris Malachowsky, external names include Jony Srouji, Rene Haas, Lisa Su, and Lip-Bu Tan. Post-news, AMD was voted the #1 new money buy idea at a semis roundtable, AVGO is positioned as heir apparent for AI chip capital allocation, and ANET had 50%+ of hardware lunch attendees calling it a Buy before the NVDA news broke.

bullets.title: Prediction Markets Pricing 90% Odds of December Fed Rate Hike; QUAD4 Transition in Play
bullets.body: Prediction markets now show 90% probability of a 25bp Fed rate hike in December 2026, up 15 percentage points week-over-week, with January 2027 at 56% odds of an additional 25bp hike. Hedgeye's macro framework frames a QUAD2→QUAD4 transition underway mid-quarter heading into 1H27, with the 30yr shifted to Bearish TREND, 10yr testing the 4.91% TREND line, and the dollar remaining Bullish TREND on relative policy divergence. Yield curve is bull flattening at the long end while front-end rates stay elevated.

bullets.title: 10-Year Yield at 5.02%; Hawkish CPI Repricing Pressures Levered Consumer Cyclicals
bullets.body: The 10-year yield is +4bps to 5.02% this morning, with 2yr yields up ~20bps over two days on hawkish repricing; Tuesday's CPI print is cited as the catalyst for higher-for-longer expectations feeding into rate hikes rather than growth. 22V Research flags consumer cyclicals with high debt as the most exposed: the basket outperformed S&P 1500 by +14% when yields fell in October but is now expected to underperform as rates stabilize higher, with valuations above long-term medians while earnings growth expectations fall.

bullets.title: Market Breadth Severely Deteriorated: NASDAQ New Lows Exceed Highs for 53 Straight Days
bullets.body: NASDAQ New Lows have outnumbered New Highs for 53 consecutive days and has recorded 69 straight days with at least 100 New Lows, yet the index has only corrected ~12% — historically shallow relative to streak length. S&P futures are +0.60% to 7595 this morning after the NVDA-led selloff, but OPCO notes S&P/QQQ volumes were 20-30% below 10-day average on yesterday's rally, QQQ IV trades at a 13% discount to 30-day realized vol, and SpotGamma flags SPX downside gamma at 7350. Defensive order flow has persisted for two weeks with the desk recommending selling rallies.

bullets.title: Existing Home Sales Collapse to 3.75M — GFC-Level Lows — as Mortgage Rates Bite
bullets.body: October existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m to a 3.75M annualized rate (vs. MS estimate 3.89M), with single-family down 5.8% m/m and 8.6% y/y — matching GFC lows and below COVID troughs; single-family annualized pace is 27% below population-adjusted historical norms. Inventories rose to cycle highs (months' supply also at cycle highs), median price growth decelerated to +0.4% y/y from +2.5% in July. PSC Macro notes housing recovery requires both lower Treasury yields AND lower rate volatility; mortgage rates can fall faster than yields if vol eases.

bullets.title: Labor Market Remains Solid: Initial Claims ~200K, 13-Week Avg Down 13% Y/Y
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims held near ~200K with the 13-week average down 13% year-over-year despite typical holiday-season noise; continuing claims are grinding lower at sub-1.7M, and the exhaustion rate rolling over signals rehiring is outpacing benefit terminations. The labor data stands in stark contrast to housing, reinforcing the bifurcated macro picture heading into potential Fed hikes.

bullets.title: CRWV +25% on $132.5B Backlog Beat; Raising $4B IG Debt to Fund AI Infrastructure
bullets.body: CoreWeave surged 25% after reporting a beat/raise with $132.5B in backlog, triggering a broader AI infrastructure rebound with the SOX ~18% off November 5 lows and NDX +2.3%. CRWV is separately seeking to raise at least $4B in investment-grade debt backed by customer contracts; Citi notes this could accrete ~$27/sh equity value through year-end 2027 via debt tender. Retail dip-buying was notable last week with leveraged equity ETF inflows of ~$5B ($15B equivalent after leverage) on November 5-6.

bullets.title: NBIS Q3: 571% Revenue Growth, 47% EBITDA Margin, 2027 Revenue Guided $12-13B — But Stock -19%
bullets.body: Nebius reported Q3 revenue of $981M, beating consensus by 9pts (+571% Y/Y), with GPU-hour pricing up >20% QoQ and new contract ACV exceeding $25M/MW vs. $20M in Q2; Q3 capex was fully covered by customer prepayments and 2027 capex ($40-45B) is 75-85% funded by prepayments and asset-backed financing. Despite the beat and 2027 revenue guide of $12-13B with pre-tax breakeven by Q4'27, the stock fell ~19% on delivery delays at Vineland NJ pushing the ARR target from December to February. Citi upgraded to Buy with a $265 PT (71% upside), citing customer concentration (MSFT+META ~40% of FY26 ARR) as key risk.

bullets.title: GPU Spot Prices Mean-Reverting; Inference Demand Favoring Older Chips as B300 Supply Hits
bullets.body: 1-year US GPU rental rates for A100/H100/H200 have reverted to mid-October levels over the past month, and B300 rental rates gave back most late-October gains. Neocloud operators are discounting B300 capacity to raise cash as equities fall and borrowing costs rise; demand is shifting from training to inference, where older Nvidia accelerators are more economical. B300/GB300 clusters are coming online from end of Q4 2026 through mid-Q1 2027, adding supply pressure.

bullets.title: Memory Makers Plan Aggressive Price Hikes: Enterprise SSD +15-20%, PC DRAM +13-18% in 4Q26
bullets.body: Memory makers are preparing new price hikes in 4Q26: Enterprise SSD +15-20% QoQ, PC DRAM +13-18% QoQ; STMicroelectronics raises prices January 1 after three prior rounds in 2026, with TXN and NXPI also implementing adjustments. OpenAI CEO Altman separately warned Samsung of double-counted demand and potential near-term volatility, adding a demand uncertainty overlay even as component suppliers push pricing higher.

bullets.title: Commerce Dept. Finalizing AI Remote Access Rule Extending Export Controls to 7 More Countries
bullets.body: The Commerce Department is reportedly finalizing an AI remote access rule extending export controls to seven additional countries including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand; Chinese AI firms are rushing to secure NVIDIA compute capacity overseas ahead of tighter restrictions. The political dynamic around NVIDIA's governance crisis is reportedly pushing Washington toward even tighter restrictions on offshore data centers serving Chinese customers, which represent ~20% of NVIDIA revenue.

bullets.title: Key Macro/Earnings Calendar: NVDA Reports Nov 17; Fed Minutes Nov 18; Retail Sales Nov 17
bullets.body: The critical near-term calendar: NVDA earnings November 17 (revenue consensus ~$109B, MS estimate ~$112B, guide $108B); Retail Sales also November 17 (YoY comparison unavailable due to October 2025 shutdown); Fed Minutes November 18 at 2pm ET; housing data (starts, permits, pending sales) November 18. Microsoft Ignite runs November 17-20 in SF, with investor focus on AI monetization, Copilot evolution, and cybersecurity (~$30B franchise). US-China trade truce extended through January 20, 2027; US government funding deadline is December 11.

bullets.title: Agentic Commerce Reaching Inflection; AMZN 400M+ Alexa Shopping Users, META Muse Scaling
bullets.body: Citi sees agentic commerce at an inflection point with Amazon's 400M+ Alexa Shopping users and META Muse scaling as the primary vectors; however, META's Muse AI agent has been blocked by eBay and United Airlines citing privacy and regulatory concerns. The broader market for AI monitoring, testing, and validation infrastructure is emerging as a spending category, with Datadog, CoreWeave (Weights & Biases), Cisco (Galileo for Splunk), and Dynatrace (Arize) all acquiring monitoring startups.

bullets.title: Macau GGR Cut -2% for 2026 and -8% for 2027; UBS Downgrades MLCO to Sell
bullets.body: UBS lowered Macau GGR estimates to $30.4B for 2026 (flat YoY) and $29.4B for 2027 (-3% YoY), cutting Q4'26 growth forecast to -10% YoY on soft Chinese macro, offshore tax enforcement, and challenging base effects. Price targets cut across the board: WYNN to $124 (Buy), LVS to $48 (Neutral), MGM to $36 (Neutral); MLCO separately downgraded to Sell with PT cut to $3.70 from $7.70, implying 16% downside.

bullets.title: AI Tech Short Interest Below Market Average Despite Selloff; Low-Short-Interest Names Outperform
bullets.body: 22V Research notes Technology sector short interest as a percent of free float remains below the S&P 500 average despite October increases, with the sector's DTC ratio the lowest among all sectors — reflecting strong liquidity rather than a broad bearish conviction call. Software saw the largest decline in short interest since mid-July; lowest short interest quintile posted the strongest annualized returns and Sharpe ratios. This suggests the AI selloff reflects momentum unwind and position reduction rather than fundamental short thesis building.

bullets.title: EU Court Backs $1.7B Google Antitrust Fine; Alphabet Asian Bond Drew $7B+ Demand
bullets.body: An EU court adviser backed a €1.7B antitrust fine against Google for anti-competitive online advertising practices, reversing a lower tribunal's 2019 decision to scrap the penalty. Separately, Alphabet's debut Asian-currency bond offering drew over $7B in demand, demonstrating strong credit appetite for the name even amid regulatory headwinds.

bullets.title: HUBS +8% on Halligan Return as CEO; Expects Aggressive Restructuring, M&A Acceleration
bullets.body: HubSpot co-founder Brian Halligan returns as CEO effective November 12, replacing Yamini Rangan; Karen Burgess (Adobe Creativity & Productivity CFO) joins as EVP Finance November 30, becoming CFO February 2027. KeyBanc sees Halligan's return as a precursor to deeper headcount cuts (peers cut 20%+), repricing/packaging strategy shift away from multi-hub to all-encompassing front-office seat model, and M&A acceleration; HUBS reaffirmed FY26 guidance and trades at 2.4x CY27 EV/revenue vs. software sector at 5.7x.

bullets.title: Texas Gambling Legalization (HJR 52) Could Be Major Catalyst for Gaming Names by Nov 2027
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags the Texas gambling legalization bill (HJR 52) as a potential catalyst for DKNG and other gaming operators if passed by November 2027. Separately, Macau/China consumer weakness and Las Vegas softness are creating broad downward pressure on gaming estimates across the sector.
